v.s: By the dawn
v.c: By the dawn,

q: (of Dhul Hijjah)! (Rasulullaah ﷺ mentioned that good deeds are more beloved to Allaah during these ten days of Dhul Hijjah than during any other time.)
v.s: And [by] ten nights
v.c: and the ten nights,

q: By the even and the odd
(all of which been created in pairs and with their opposite partners)!
v.s: And [by] the even [number] and the odd
v.c: and the even and the odd,

q: By the night when it departs!
v.s: And [by] the night when it passes,
v.c: and the night when it passes!

q: Is there not an oath in this for the intelligent?

(Are these oaths not sufficient for the intelligent? These oaths are taken to strengthen the assertion that declares: “Those who adamantly reject the message of Islaam are inviting Allaah's punishment to themselves and will be destroyed just as previous nations were destroyed when they rejected the message of their Ambiyaa.)
v.s: Is there [not] in [all] that an oath [sufficient] for one of perception?
v.c: Is all this ˹not˺ a sufficient oath for those who have sense?

q: Have you not seen how your Rabb dealt with the Aad
(who were destroyed by a terrible windstorm)...
v.s: Have you not considered how your Lord dealt with ʿAad -
v.c: Did you not see how your Lord dealt with ’Ȃd—

v.s: [With] Iram - who had lofty pillars,
v.c: ˹the people˺ of Iram—with ˹their˺ great stature,

q: were not created in the lands.
v.s: The likes of whom had never been created in the land?
v.c: unmatched in any other land;

q: (Have you not also seen how your Rabb dealt with)
The Thamud who used to carve the rocks of the valley
(to make their homes in the mountains)?
v.s: And [with] Thamūd, who carved out the rocks in the valley?
v.c: and Thamûd who carved ˹their homes into˺ the rocks in the ˹Stone˺ Valley;

q: (have you not also seen how your Rabb dealt with)
Fir'oun, the lord of the stakes
v.s: And [with] Pharaoh, owner of the stakes?
v.c: and the Pharaoh of mighty structures?

v.s: [All of] whom oppressed within the lands
v.c: They all transgressed throughout the land,

v.s: And increased therein the corruption.
v.c: spreading much corruption there.

q: your Rabb rained punishment on them.
v.s: So your Lord poured upon them a scourge of punishment.
v.c: So your Lord unleashed on them a scourge of punishment.

q: Verily your Rabb is Ever Vigilant
v.s: Indeed, your Lord is in observation.
v.c: ˹For˺ your Lord is truly vigilant.

q: (instead of learning from the incidents of the past, he takes no heed and)
(to see whether he is grateful to Allaah)
by granting him honour and favours, he says, “My Rabb has honoured me
(because I am His chosen one and deserve this).” (Instead of expressing thanks to Allaah and using the wealth and favours in a manner that pleases Allaah, he becomes proud and conceited.)
v.s: And as for man, when his Lord tries him and [thus] is generous to him and favors him, he says, “My Lord has honoured me.”
v.c: Now, whenever a human being is tested by their Lord through ˹His˺ generosity and blessings, they boast, “My Lord has ˹deservedly˺ honoured me!”

q: (He therefore fails the test by complaining and thereafter flouting Allaah's commands in a desperate effort to acquire some wealth.)
v.s: But when He tries him and restricts his provision, he says, "My Lord has humiliated me."
v.c: But when He tests them by limiting their provision, they protest, “My Lord has ˹undeservedly˺ humiliated me!”

q: (A shortage in one's sustenance does not indicate rejection by Allaah, just as an increase in sustenance does not indicate acceptance by Him.)
(apart from being a test for you, your sustenance is sometimes decreased as a form of punishment because)
you do not honour the orphan
v.s: No! But you do not honour the orphan
v.c: Absolutely not! In fact, you are not ˹even˺ gracious to the orphan,

q: ...do not encourage feeding of the poor...
v.s: And you do not encourage one another to feed the poor.
v.c: nor do you urge one another to feed the poor.

q: (of others, especially of women and orphans)
v.s: And you consume inheritance, devouring [it] altogether,
v.c: And you devour ˹others’˺ inheritance greedily,

q: you love wealth with a very deep love
(which reduces and eventually destroys your love for Allaah and causes you to commit greater sins).
v.s: And you love wealth with immense love.
v.c: and love wealth fervently.

q: (You should never think that these acts do not warrant Allaah's punishment. They certainly do! If not already meted out in this world, this punishment will definitely arrive on that Day of Qiyaamah)
When the earth shall be ripped to shreds
v.s: No! When the earth has been leveled - pounded and crushed
v.c: Enough! When the earth is entirely crushed over and over,

q: when your Rabb shall commence proceedings
v.s: And your Lord has come and the angels, rank upon rank,
v.c: and your Lord comes ˹to judge˺ with angels, rank upon rank,

q: ...and the day when Jahannam will be brought to the fore
On that day man will understand
(the errors of his ways in this world).
But of what use will this understanding be
(because it will be too late to make amends)?
v.s: And brought [within view], that Day, is Hell - that Day, man will remember, but how [i.e., what good] to him will be the remembrance?
v.c: and Hell is brought forth on that Day—this is when every ˹disbelieving˺ person will remember ˹their own sins˺. But what is the use of remembering then?

q: will say, “Oh dear! If only I had sent
v.s: He will say, "Oh, I wish I had sent ahead [some good] for my life."
v.c: They will cry, “I wish I had sent forth ˹something good˺ for my ˹true˺ life.”

q: So on that day, none shall punish like His
v.s: So on that Day, none will punish [as severely] as His punishment,
v.c: On that Day He will punish ˹them˺ severely, like no other,

v.s: And none will bind [as severely] as His binding [of the evildoers].
v.c: and bind ˹them˺ tightly, like no other.

q: (As for the sincere and devout Mu'mineen, Allaah will say to each of them,)
v.s: [To the righteous it will be said], "O reassured soul,
v.c: ˹Allah will say to the righteous,˺ “O tranquil soul!

q: to your Rabb as He is
v.s: Return to your Lord, well-pleased and pleasing [to Him],
v.c: Return to your Lord, well pleased ˹with Him˺ and well pleasing ˹to Him˺.

v.s: And enter among My [righteous] servants
v.c: So join My servants,

v.s: And enter My Paradise."
v.c: and enter My Paradise.”
